title: State machines and logic families
kicker: ENEX 152 · Digital Logic · Sequential Machine Design and Digital ICs
subtitle: Turn a behaviour described in words into states, a transition table and finally flip-flops and gates — then meet the silicon it runs on.

sections.title: Finite state machines
sections.body: A finite state machine has a set of states, inputs, a next-state rule and outputs. In a Moore machine the output depends only on the state; in a Mealy machine on state and input (so it can react a clock earlier and may need fewer states). A state diagram draws states as circles and transitions as labelled arrows.

sections.title: A sequence detector
sections.body: Design a detector that raises its output when the input ends in 11. States: q0 (no progress), q1 (last bit was a 1), q2 (saw 11). On input 1 move forward (q0→q1→q2, and q2 stays); on input 0 fall back to q0. The machine accepts yes for 0110111 (final q2) and no for 0101 (final q1).

questions.prompt: With overlapping detection, after seeing “111” the machine should be in…

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: The last two bits are still 11.

sections.title: From diagram to circuit
sections.body: 1) Draw the state diagram. 2) Assign binary codes to states (n flip-flops for up to 2ⁿ states). 3) Write the state table: present state, input → next state, output. 4) Use each flip-flop’s excitation table to get input equations; simplify them with K-maps. 5) Draw the circuit and check unused states go somewhere safe.

problems.prompt: A traffic-light controller has 6 states. How many flip-flops with binary coding, and how many codes are unused?
problems.answer: 3 flip-flops; 2³ − 6 = 2 unused codes (design them to return to a valid state).

sections.title: Logic families and their numbers
sections.body: Gates are built in families. TTL (bipolar, 5 V) is fast but power-hungry; CMOS (complementary MOSFETs) uses almost no power except when switching and is the basis of all modern chips. Key figures: propagation delay (how long an output takes to change), power dissipation, noise margin (NM = VIH − VOH style gap between output and input thresholds) and fan-out (how many inputs one output can drive).

worked.why: A gate outputs at least 4.0 V for a 1 and the next gate accepts any input ≥ 3.5 V as 1.

questions.prompt: A larger noise margin means the circuit…

choices.text: Tolerates more noise before misreading a bit.

sections.title: CMOS inverter and NAND
sections.body: A CMOS inverter is a PMOS (pull-up to VDD) over an NMOS (pull-down to ground) sharing gate and output: input 0 turns the PMOS on, output 1; input 1 turns the NMOS on, output 0. Only one conducts in steady state, so static power is near zero; power is spent charging and discharging load capacitance: P = C·V²·f. A NAND puts two NMOS in series and two PMOS in parallel.

worked.why: C = 10 pF, V = 3.3 V, f = 50 MHz.
Dynamic power P = C V² f.

questions.prompt: Why does CMOS use almost no static power?

choices.text: One transistor of the pair is always off.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: No steady path from VDD to ground.

figures.caption: Figure 5.5.1 — CMOS inverter
figures.note: With input 0 the PMOS connects the output to VDD.
figures.script:
diagram("direction: down
[VDD] as v
[PMOS: on when input = 0] as p
[Output] as o
[NMOS: on when input = 1] as n
[Ground] as g
v -> p
p -> o
o -> n
n -> g
@0 v -> p
@1 p -> o : input 0 → out 1
loop 1");

problems.prompt: Halving the supply voltage of a CMOS chip (same C and f) changes dynamic power by what factor?

sections.title: Programmable logic and memory
sections.body: Instead of wiring gates, load a configuration: a ROM is a look-up table (2ⁿ words of m bits implement any m functions of n inputs); a PLA/PAL programs AND and OR planes; an FPGA has thousands of small look-up tables and flip-flops joined by programmable routing. Memory: SRAM (flip-flop cell, fast, 6 transistors) vs DRAM (capacitor, dense, refreshed).

worked.why: A 4-input look-up table stores one output bit for each input pattern.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It stores the full 64-row truth table.
